title: Jorgensen 2003b: centroid distance of paraspinal / lumbar extensor mass at L5-S1 (M, lateral_recumbent)
muscle_as_reported: right lumbar erector muscle mass (longissimus, iliocostalis, multifidus)

imaging.plane: axial slices through and PARALLEL to each lumbar disc (T12-L1..L5-S1)
imaging.posture_detail: lateral recumbent (left side down), torso flexion 0/15/30/45 deg

quantity.name: centroid_distance
quantity.definition: distance from the vertebral-body (or disc) centroid to the muscle area centroid in the image plane; AP signed (+ anterior, - posterior), ML unsigned lateral distance. NOT a true moment arm

source.authors: Jorgensen MJ, Marras WS, Gupta P, Waters TR
source.sample: 24 healthy subjects (12 M, 12 F); same subjects/scans as Jorgensen 2003a

protocol.summary: Distance between disc centroid and right erector muscle group centroid in the sagittal direction defined by the disc centroid-spinous process line.
how_to_simulate: Put the model lateral recumbent with 15 deg torso flexion; match the measured lumbar lordosis (L1-S1 31.4 deg, L1-L5 26.7 deg).
Cut a plane through the L5-S1 disc centroid parallel to the disc mid-plane.
Take the PCSA-weighted centroid of the RIGHT longissimus + iliocostalis + multifidus fascicles in that plane.
Report its distance from the disc centroid along the line disc centroid -> spinous process (sagittal/AP direction; measured as positive posterior, stored here as negative = posterior).
protocol.notes: Authors call it the sagittal plane moment arm; it is a centroid distance. Only the right side was digitised (left side deformed by lying on it). Table 4 (% change from neutral) is derived from Table 3 and not stored.

data.note: sign flipped: printed as positive distance posterior of disc centroid

extraction.check_notes: Table 3 layout unambiguous; all 48 values re-read against the PDF text.
